claims.evidence: Photo 0 and 1 show a three-tier console with a gold logo, consistent with a PS4 Pro.
Photos show the exterior, but internal condition and wear on components cannot be confirmed.
The warranty seals on the rear of the consoles are not shown.
Thermal performance cannot be assessed through static photos.
The witness report explicitly states rear ports were not shown.
The witness report states game controllers were not shown.
No documentation or receipts are visible in the report.

risks.risk: Consoles may have the 'Blue Light of Death' (BLOD) or other boot failures.
risks.proof: A video clip showing both consoles booting to the PlayStation home screen.

risks.risk: The consoles may have been opened or tampered with internally.
risks.proof: Clear, close-up photos of the factory warranty seals over the screw holes on the rear.

risks.risk: The controllers (pads) may be missing, third-party, or faulty.
risks.proof: A photo of the controllers and a video showing them syncing and navigating the menu.

risks.risk: HDMI or USB ports may be physically damaged or non-functional.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the front USB ports and the rear HDMI ports.

proof_requests: Video of both consoles (Slim and Pro) powering on and displaying a signal on a TV.
Photos of the game controllers mentioned by the seller.
Photos of the rear of both consoles showing the ports and warranty seals.
A photo of the UK receipt mentioned.
A screenshot of the 'System Information' screen for both consoles to verify storage capacity.
response.reason: The witness has identified the specific models (PS4 Slim and PS4 Pro), allowing for a valuation at the worst-case scenario of non-functional, standalone units.
